problems.title: An exponential equation becomes a quadratic
problems.question: Find the sum of the solutions of 8·9ˣ-30·6ˣ+27·4ˣ=0.
problems.idea: Divide by positive 4ˣ, then substitute a single exponential.
steps: The quadratic gives t=9/4 or t=3/2.
Since 9/4=(3/2)², the first solution is x=2.
The second solution is x=1. Both are valid and the sum is 3.

problems.title: Draw a specified five-letter word
problems.question: Seven balls carry letters a,a,a,i,v,sh,l. Five are drawn in order without replacement. Find the probability of forming the Georgian word “vashli” (v-a-sh-l-i, meaning apple).
problems.idea: Multiply the five conditional draw probabilities.
formulas: P(ordered sequence)=product of successive conditional probabilities.
steps: The first required letter v has probability 1/7.
The a then has probability 3/6, followed by sh with probability 1/5, l with 1/4, and i with 1/3.
problems.note: The word and the letter sh are read directly from the scan; a text transcription can misread sh as m.

problems.title: Total area from a face inclination
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has base side √3 and each lateral face makes 30° with the base. Find total surface area.
problems.idea: The lateral faces project onto the base with the same cosine factor.
formulas: For common face angle θ, B=Lcosθ, where L is lateral area.
steps: The base area is 3√3/4.
The lateral area is B/cos30°=(3√3/4)/(√3/2)=3/2.

problems.title: Even numbers formed from five different digits
problems.question: How many five-digit even numbers use each of 2,3,5,7,8 exactly once?
problems.idea: An even number must end in 2 or 8.
formulas: There are n! permutations of n distinct digits.
steps: Choose the last digit: two choices.
The remaining four digits may appear in any order: 4!=24 arrangements.
No digit is zero, so there is no leading-digit restriction. The total is 2·24=48.

problems.title: Prism height from an isosceles trapezoid base
problems.question: A right prism has an isosceles trapezoid base with parallel sides 4,6. A leg of the trapezoid is perpendicular to a diagonal. The prism volume is 25√2. Find its lateral edge.
problems.idea: Use trapezoid symmetry to recover its altitude, then divide volume by base area.
formulas: Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero.
steps: Place lower vertices at (-3,0),(3,0) and upper ones at (-2,t),(2,t).
At the upper-left vertex, a leg direction is (-1,-t) and a diagonal direction is (5,-t). Their dot product is -5+t²=0, so t=√5.
The base area is (4+6)√5/2=5√5.
The right prism’s lateral edge is its height: 25√2/(5√5)=√10.

problems.title: Count intersections of increasing and decreasing graphs
problems.question: How many real solutions does 199ˣ=10-x have?
problems.idea: The left side strictly increases and the right side strictly decreases.
formulas: For base a>1, aˣ is continuous and strictly increasing.
A continuous function changing sign on an interval has a root.
steps: Consider F(x)=199ˣ+x-10. Both variable terms increase, so F is strictly increasing and has at most one zero.
Continuity gives a zero between 0 and 1. Hence there is exactly one solution.

problems.title: A union probability needs dependence information
problems.question: The probability of rain tomorrow is 0.6; the probability of Barcelona winning the Champions League is 0.8. Find the probability that at least one occurs.
problems.idea: Use inclusion-exclusion and identify the unstated independence assumption.
steps: Write the union probability as 1.4-P(A∩B).
The given probabilities alone allow intersection values from 0.4 to 0.6, so the union can be anywhere from 0.8 to 1.
If the intended assumption is independence, the intersection is 0.6·0.8=0.48 and the union is 0.92.
problems.answer: With independence: 0.92 (option დ). Without that assumption: any value in [0.8,1].
problems.note: The printed question does not explicitly state independence. Different subject matter alone is not a mathematical proof of independence.

problems.title: A triangular section cutting off a cube corner
problems.question: A cube has volume 8. Find the section through the three other endpoints of the three edges from one vertex.
problems.idea: The section is an equilateral triangle whose sides are cube-face diagonals.
formulas: Cube volume a³; face diagonal a√2.
steps: The cube edge is a=2.
Each side of the section is 2√2, by Pythagoras in a square face.
The area is √3·(2√2)²/4=2√3.

problems.title: Respect the principal inverse-sine interval
problems.question: Find arcsin(cos(-31π/6)).
problems.idea: Reduce the inner angle first, then select the sine inverse in [-π/2,π/2].
steps: The angle in the principal inverse-sine interval with that sine is -π/3.
Angles such as 4π/3 have the same sine but are outside the inverse function’s range.

problems.title: Seat four girls with no adjacent pair
problems.question: Four boys and four girls sit randomly in a row. Find the probability that no two girls sit together.
problems.idea: Place the boys first, then put girls in distinct gaps.
formulas: All eight distinct students have 8! equally likely orders.
Four boys create five gaps: before, between, and after them.
steps: Order the boys in 4! ways.
Choose four of the five gaps for the girls, in choose(5,4)=5 ways. At most one girl per gap prevents adjacency.
Order the four girls in the chosen gaps in 4! ways.
The probability is 4!·5·4!/8!=1/14.

problems.title: Height above a 3–4–5 triangle
problems.question: Point O is 9 cm from each side of a triangle with sides 3,4,5 cm. Find its distance to the triangle’s plane.
problems.idea: Project O into the plane. In the intended interior projection, its foot is the incenter.
formulas: Distance to a side squared=height²+in-plane side distance².
steps: Let H be the perpendicular projection of O. Equal spatial side distances give equal in-plane side distances from H.
For the incenter, those distances are 1. Therefore 9²=h²+1².
Thus h=√80=4√5 cm.
problems.answer: $4\sqrt5$ cm (option დ), for the intended incenter projection.
problems.note: If “sides” means the entire supporting lines and an exterior projection is allowed, excentres give other heights: √77,6√2,3√5. The interior interpretation yields the listed intended answer; distances to the actual three side segments force an interior projection.

problems.title: A triangular prism with square lateral faces
problems.question: A regular triangular prism has a square lateral face and volume 27√3/4. Find its base side.
problems.idea: The square condition makes prism height equal base side.
steps: Let the base side be a. A lateral face has sides a and h, so being a square means h=a.
The volume is a³√3/4.
Equate it to 27√3/4 to obtain a³=27, hence a=3.

problems.title: Identify a decreasing exponential function
problems.question: Which listed function decreases on [-1,4]? The relevant candidate is y=(1+sin(π/9))^(2-x).
problems.idea: Its base exceeds one, while the exponent decreases as x increases.
formulas: For a>1, aᵗ increases with t.
steps: The base 1+sin(π/9) is greater than 1.
When x increases, 2-x decreases. Applying the increasing exponential to a decreasing exponent makes the function decrease.
The other choices increase on [-1,4]: the positive-slope lines, 8ˣ, 0.8^(-x)=(1.25)ˣ, and (x+3)²+1 with x+3≥2.

problems.title: Sine range over a long interval
problems.question: Find the range of y=sinx for x∈[π/2,11π/6].
problems.idea: The interval contains both a maximum and a minimum point of sine.
steps: The left endpoint π/2 gives 1.
The interior point 3π/2 belongs to the interval and gives -1.
Continuity provides every value between these extremes.

problems.title: A binomial coefficient with a fractional factor
problems.question: Which listed term occurs in (1+x/2)⁶?
problems.idea: The coefficient of xᵏ is choose(6,k)/2ᵏ.
steps: For k=3, the coefficient is choose(6,3)/8=20/8=5/2.
Thus (5/2)x³ occurs.
For comparison, the x,x²,x⁴,x⁵ coefficients are 3,15/4,15/16,3/16, so the other listed terms do not match.

problems.title: Find a point on an exponential graph
problems.question: y=2^(3x+k) passes through (0,4). Point A is on the graph, B=(1,199), and AB is parallel to the y-axis. Find A.
problems.idea: Use the y-intercept to find k, then use the common x-coordinate of a vertical line.
formulas: A vertical line has constant x-coordinate.
steps: At x=0 the equation gives 2ᵏ=4, hence k=2.
The vertical line through B has x=1, so A also has x=1.
Then yA=2^(3+2)=32. The value 199 fixes B’s height, not A’s.

problems.title: Square a radical inequality only after checking signs
problems.question: Solve √(2x+3)≤x.
problems.idea: The right side must be nonnegative before squaring.
formulas: A real square root is nonnegative.
steps: Require x≥0. This also ensures 2x+3≥0.
Square to get 2x+3≤x², or (x-3)(x+1)≥0.
The squared inequality gives x≤-1 or x≥3. Intersect with x≥0 to retain only x≥3.
At x=3 both sides equal 3, so the endpoint is included.

problems.title: Test integer radian angles in an absolute-value inequality
problems.question: Which of -1,1,2,3,4,5 satisfies |sinx|≤|cosx|? Angles are in radians.
problems.idea: Squaring both sides turns the test into the sign of cos2x.
steps: For x=-1 or 1, cos2x=cos2<0; for x=2, cos4<0.
For x=3, cos6>0 because 6 is in quadrant IV.
For x=4, reduce 8 by 2π: the angle is in quadrant II, so cos8<0. For x=5, reduce 10 by 2π: it is in quadrant III, so cos10<0.
Only x=3 passes the test.

problems.title: A ratio does not determine an absolute size
problems.question: A rectangular box’s lateral area is four times its base area. Can its lateral area, base area, volume, height or diagonal-section area be determined numerically?
problems.idea: The condition is preserved by scaling every dimension.
formulas: For base sides a,b and height h: L=2(a+b)h, B=ab.
steps: There is no given value for either a or b. For instance, a=b=1 gives h=1, while a=b=2 gives h=2.
Both boxes satisfy the condition, but their areas, volumes and heights differ.
Uniform scaling also changes every diagonal-section area. None of the listed absolute quantities is fixed.
problems.answer: None of the preceding quantities can be determined (option ვ).

problems.title: Order edge, apothem and diagonal angles
problems.question: In a regular square pyramid, α is the angle of a lateral edge with the base, β the angle of an apothem with the base, and γ the angle between base diagonals. Order them.
problems.idea: The apothem has a shorter horizontal projection than the edge, and the square’s diagonals are perpendicular.
formulas: For base side a and height h: tanα=h/(a/√2), tanβ=h/(a/2).
steps: The projection a/√2 is larger than a/2, so tanα<tanβ and α<β.
Both are acute angles because the pyramid height and base size are positive.
The square diagonals make γ=90°, which is larger than either.

problems.title: Distance between two cube-edge midpoints
problems.question: A cube has volume 8 cm³. M is the midpoint of A1B1 and N of AD. Find MN.
problems.idea: Use coordinates with cube edge 2.
steps: The edge length is 2 cm.

problems.title: Volume from three face areas
problems.question: A rectangular box has its three different face areas equal to 4,6,8. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Their product is the square of the volume.
steps: Multiply the face areas: 4·6·8=192.
Take the positive square root because volume is positive.

problems.title: Closest multiple of a vector
problems.question: a=(1,1,-1), b=(2,3,-1). Find real k making |b-ka| as small as possible.
problems.idea: Minimise the squared length, which is a quadratic in k.
steps: The squared length is 3k²-12k+14=3(k-2)²+2.
Its minimum occurs at k=2; taking a square root does not change the minimising k.

problems.title: Match exponents using a common base
problems.question: Solve (1/36)^(1.25x-2)=6.
problems.idea: Write 1/36 as 6⁻² and 1.25 as 5/4.
steps: Solve: 5x/2=3, so x=6/5.

problems.title: Which real powers exceed one?
problems.question: Which exceed 1: a=8^(sin2), b=(√3-1)^(sin3), c=(√3+1)^(√3-1), d=(tan(π/3))^(tan(2π/3))?
problems.idea: Compare each positive base to one and determine its exponent’s sign.
formulas: For base A>1, Aᵗ>1 iff t>0; for 0<A<1 the inequality reverses.
steps: a has base greater than 1 and positive exponent, so a>1.
b has base √3-1 between 0 and 1 and positive exponent, so b<1.
c has base greater than 1 and positive exponent, so c>1.
d has base √3>1 and negative exponent, so d<1.
